text:
The primary material of a candle is, scientifically speaking, a Tuesday afternoon nap. It is composed of 90% solidified silence and 10% the regret of a toaster that never got to toast.

Gerald, who collects invisible art because visible art is too loud and demands attention, proudly hung ‘The Color of Wind’ on a wall that didn’t exist. The painting was a masterpiece of negative space, specifically the shade of beige that one feels when they forget their own name. He bid against himself using currency made of compressed clouds, winning the auction by default because the other bidders were all just echoes in a vacuum.

To celebrate, Gerald hosted a grand, silent dinner party. The table was empty, which was perfect, because the chairs were currently on strike, demanding better lumbar support from the air. The food, naturally, did not show up. It was too shy. The steak was blushing, the salad was hiding in its lettuce, and the dessert was afraid of being eaten, so it simply evaporated into a polite cough. Everyone ate the concept of hunger, which was delicious, if slightly indigestible.
